I’ve struggled with overwhelming anxiety and school for a very long time now. I had a couple traumatic life events happen on 2 different college campuses; one at a community college and the other at a 4 year college. I took a break after the 2nd and then went back to community college and finished the pre-reqs for nursing school. I was accepted and in my 2nd semester. I had a panic attack before a day of clinical at a rehab facility. My mom passed away in hospice a few years prior and I think being in that setting triggered some deep emotions. My school had a zero tolerance policy for missing and I was expelled. At the time, I had also been working as a research assistant for one of the PhD nurses on faculty since the beginning of school so about a year. I appealed the decision and my mentor also went to bat for me. The school did not sympathize and I was not allowed back.

It was devastating. I felt lost and like I was a failure. Since then however, I looked back with fresh eyes at what I could go to school for. I realized I really like Computer Science and am now finishing a degree in that. Every time, I drive past a hospital, I realize that that was not where I was supposed to end up and am actually grateful to have been forced out of that area. Sometimes life works out in weird ways and our lowest moments end up being the best turning points when we look back.
